clue.text: Gentle criminal a guard left

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters of these words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered crook turns out to be a security guard who has just walked off the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns A GUARD into GRADUA; L for left follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle slope or change is a slow, gradual one, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Grabbing grass under golf trolley's bottom

indicators.note: under means the grass word is placed below the letter for golf in this down answer

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: bottom means the last letter of the word, in a down entry

explanation.surface: Grass is caught under the bottom of a golf trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts REED below G; Y is the last letter of 'trolley's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone grasping or grabbing wants more than their share, a synonym of avaricious.

clue.text: Venerable Roman emperor ignores us

indicators.note: ignores means leaving out, so the letters of us are dropped from the emperor's name

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An aged and revered Roman ruler takes no notice of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' removes the final US from AUGUSTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dignified and worthy of respect, much like venerable.

clue.text: Coped with next EU changes dismissing nothing not bargained for

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into another order
dismissing means sending away, so the letter for nothing leaves the word coped

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone handled the next set of European Union reforms, which got rid of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes O (nothing) from COPED, leaving CPED; 'changes' rearranges CPED with NEXT EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not bargained for is a surprise, a synonym of unforeseen.

clue.text: Accommodate novelist

definitions.meaning: to accommodate is to house someone for a time
David ... is an English novelist, author of Small World and Nice Work

explanation.definitionFit: To lodge guests is to house them, and David Lodge is the English author of comic campus novels.

clue.text: Exercise reduced in vain

parts.note: to exercise a right or power is to use it
something reduced is less than before

explanation.surface: Cutting down on workouts proves pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort made in vain achieves nothing, which is a synonym for being futile or of no use.

clue.text: Rue Andrew's tight thong, perhaps

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Andrew regrets how snug his skimpy thong is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like a description of the thong but means drunk, rearranging RUE ANDREW; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is an example of skimpy clothing worn beneath outer garments, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Every coach beginning to leave

indicators.note: the beginning of the word leaves, so its first letter goes

parts.note: to coach someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: Every bus starts to pull away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus but is the verb TEACH, which loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both mean all of a group, taken one by one.

clue.text: One trust supporting hospital department in full

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so in this down answer the hospital department sits above

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
I is the Roman numeral one
to rely on someone is to trust them

explanation.surface: A single health trust props up a hospital department completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts I and RELY beneath ENT, the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in full means completely, wholly, without leaving any part out.

clue.text: Furtive fish goes between rocks

indicators.note: goes between means the fish is placed inside the word for rocks

parts.note: something that rocks sways from side to side
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A shifty fish slips between some rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun for stones, but it is a verb meaning moves to and fro; 'goes between' puts the fish inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A furtive glance is a sly, sideways look, sneaked from the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Texan golfer occasionally could see this?

definitions.text: Texan golfer occasionally could see this?

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of these two words is taken

explanation.surface: A golfer from Texas might now and then score two under par on a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of TEXAN GOLFER spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes what a golfer may sometimes achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a score of two strokes under par on a hole is named after a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Loyal cadet died fighting

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle that throws these letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A faithful young officer trainee lost his life in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges CADET DIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal supporter is committed and devoted, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Harry said soft fruit goes off

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or worry, so the letters of the word said are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry reports that the squashy fruit has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads like a name but is the anagram signal, a verb meaning harass. 'goes off' looks like fruit spoiling but means leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to leave and vanish from sight, a synonym of vanishes.

clue.text: Boast about fight

parts.note: C (circa) is the abbreviation for about, as with dates
a row is a noisy quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a scrap they were in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link but supplies C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow over something is to gloat or brag about it, a synonym of boast.

clue.text: Having astronomical vision?

parts.note: astronomical suggests something huge or dreamy, but here it means looking at the heavens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Astronomical' reads as 'enormous', as in visionary daydreaming, but literally it means watching the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Peering at the night sky through a telescope is literally observing the heavens, and the word also means daydreaming.

clue.text: Stress about identification friend produces by mistake

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for stress wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: an accent is stress placed on a syllable
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Pressure over a security check from a pal leads to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' here is the emphasis on a syllable, not anxiety; 'about' wraps it round the abbreviation for identification. 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unintentionally happens by mistake, so the adverb and the phrase are synonyms.

clue.text: This writer is turning out to be getting better

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself says I am, shortened to I'm
proving means turning out to be, as in proving difficult

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be on the mend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so 'This writer is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient getting better is on the mend, a synonym of recovering.

clue.text: Hold cutting tool

definitions.meaning: in wrestling, a hold in which the legs are locked round an opponent
a pair of crossing blades used for cutting paper or cloth

explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler's leg-lock hold is named after the bladed cutter, and the cutter itself is the everyday tool.

clue.text: Manoeuvre train with sign of hesitation

parts.note: a railway engine pulls a train, so it stands for it here
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone shunts a train about, pausing uncertainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre' looks like the action on the train, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to contrive or manoeuvre it into happening, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Latest Conservative: here today, gone tomorrow

parts.note: something here today and gone tomorrow lasts only a short while, so it is temporary

explanation.surface: The newest Tory politician is a fleeting presence, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibes at short-lived politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern, up-to-date designs can be called the latest, a synonym of current or modern.

clue.text: Some climbing cedar — it's generating angry harangue

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something scaling a cedar tree stirs up a furious outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'generating angry harangue' as the definition, but 'generating' is a link word: the definition is 'angry harangue'. 'climbing' reverses EDARIT, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, furious speech of denunciation is a rant, which is what the word names.

clue.text: English golfer, a lefty

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: An English golfer happens to play left-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lefty' looks like a left-handed golfer, but means a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels, co-author of The Communist Manifesto, was a man of the political left.

clue.text: Businessman's clubs?

definitions.meaning: a businessman is informally called after the formal clothes he wears to work
clubs is one of the four sets in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: The clue asks whether a businessman owns golf clubs or nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests golf or nightclubs, but means one of the four card sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Office workers are nicknamed for their formal jackets and trousers, and clubs is one of the four card divisions, hearts and spades being others.

clue.text: Platoon I ordered to protect most of bar's inhabitants

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the rearranged letters go round the shortened bar
ordered means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to guard most of a bar full of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges PLATOON I into POLATION, and 'to protect' places the shortened bar inside that, after its first two letters. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The people living in a place, taken together, form its population, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Swelling — not small — daughter prodded

indicators.note: not means the letter for small is left out of the word for swelling

parts.note: a surge is a swelling rise, as of the sea
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter is nudged about a lump that is not small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swelling' suggests a lump, but here it is a rush or rise like a wave; 'not' takes out its small letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be urged on is to be pushed or nudged, a past-tense synonym of prodded.

clue.text: A large island south of Borneo, primarily?

definitions.text: A large island south of Borneo, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: The clue describes a big island lying below Borneo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' puts the opening letter of Borneo above the opening letters of A, LARGE, ISLAND in this down entry, and the whole clue describes the Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian holiday island lies to the south of Borneo, across the Java Sea.

clue.text: Ordinary exercises sailor's managing

parts.note: PE (physical education) means exercises
a rating is a sailor who is not an officer

explanation.surface: A regular sailor is in charge of the workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: A RATING is a non-commissioned sailor in the Royal Navy. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Running or managing a business is operating it, so the participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Annoyed thief on a boat losing power

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word for a thief at sea

parts.note: a pirate is a robber at sea
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A pirate who has lost his strength is not happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes P (power) from PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being angry or annoyed is a synonym of being cross.

clue.text: One on the board is doing this in the main?

definitions.text: One on the board is doing this in the main?

parts.words: One on the board is doing this in the main?
parts.note: 'board' suggests a company board, but here it is a board ridden on waves, and 'the main' is the sea

explanation.surface: A board member is asked what they mostly do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the board' and 'in the main' read as company director and 'mostly'; really they are a wave rider's board and the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding waves standing on a board out at sea is the water sport described.

clue.text: Pointed looks start to distract cricket commentator?

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: Aggers is the nickname of Jonathan Agnew, the BBC cricket commentator

explanation.surface: A cricket broadcaster gets glared at for putting a player off.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGERS is Jonathan Agnew, a well-known BBC radio cricket commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: To look daggers at someone is an idiom for glaring at them with hostility.
